title: RELAY v4 command bus
description: Generated from crates/relay-bus by `relay schema`. Do not edit; see docs/BUS.md.

bus.ops.summary: List ops with registry attributes, filtered to what the actor may call

bus.whoami.summary: Who am I and what may I call — for any actor, agent or not

bus.unsubscribe.summary: Stop receiving events on this connection

app.status.summary: Engine status: paths, live sessions, providers

app.quit.summary: Quit the engine; conflict app.sessions_live unless force

app.resources.get.summary: Per-pane RAM/CPU, per-worktree disk, store size

app.resources.watch.summary: While any client watches, resource.sample events flow; otherwise none

app.recovery.last.summary: What crash recovery did at the last launch

app.log.tail.summary: Reserved: emits app.log.attached and sends no log frames yet; the engine logs to relay serve's output (RELAY_LOG filters it)

app.backup.now.summary: Copy store.db to the backup dir now; keep last 5

app.import.v3.summary: One-time import of a v3 .relay/relay.db into a project

app.first_run.state.summary: First-run wizard state: workspace / providers / project / import

app.reconcile.summary: Run the trust-but-verify pass now: retention of soft-deleted rows, notifications and mail

audit.get.summary: One audit row with its stored payload

audit.undo.summary: Replay the inverse of an audited op; conflict audit.stale if the entity changed since

workspace.create.summary: Register a directory as a workspace

workspace.discover.summary: Resolve a workspace path and discover Git repositories inside it

workspace.remove.summary: Forget a workspace; conflict if it still has projects unless force removes them too

project.add.summary: Register a git repo inside a workspace as a project

project.clone.summary: Clone a repo into the workspace and register it (async; project.changed when done)

project.remove.summary: Forget a project (repository untouched); conflict if live sessions unless force closes them

task.get.summary: One task with attachments and commits

task.activity.summary: Task-scoped audit history and explicitly associated messages, newest first

task.list.summary: Tasks, filtered; project_id optional for cross-project views

task.update.summary: Patch a task (agents: own task, body/changelog only)

task.move.summary: Move a task to a column (agents: own task, active→in_review only)

task.link_commit.summary: Link a commit sha to a task

task.changelog.write.summary: Write the sentence that ships in patch notes

task.attach.summary: Attach an image by bytes or by path

task.parent.set.summary: Promote a task into a sub-task, re-parent it, or detach it

task.children.summary: Direct children in board order, or the whole subtree

task.label.add.summary: Tag a task, creating the project label if it is new

task.label.list.summary: Every label in the project, alphabetical

task.relate.summary: Record blocked_by or duplicate_of; stored and rendered, not enforced

task.unrelate.summary: Drop a blocked_by or duplicate_of edge

task.dispatch.summary: Send or stage a task; fanout sends its sub-tasks too

task.approve.summary: open task → done, linking the commit

task.copy_text.summary: The copy-button text: title + body + id

module.complete.summary: Archive a module and stamp the date

module.delete.summary: Soft-delete a module; its tasks keep existing unlinked

module.changelog.draft.summary: Draft patch notes from done tasks' changelog fields

notes.append.summary: Append text to a note, the project's standing note, or its agent suggestions note

notes.standing.summary: Exactly what gets injected at dispatch

mailbox.send.summary: Send normal or priority mail to a session name, or normal mail to * (broadcast); reaches every provider

mailbox.outbox.summary: Messages this actor sent, with each addressee's state

session.create.summary: Allocate a session (name, worktree, token); spawns nothing

session.spawn.summary: Start the provider CLI in the worktree with the brief

session.clear_restorable.summary: Fresh-spawn a restorable session without its saved provider context

session.wake.summary: Respawn a parked session with provider resume

session.close.summary: Kill, purge build output, remove worktree; branch kept

session.intent.summary: Declare in one line what this session is doing; peers read it in session.peers

session.list.summary: Sessions, filtered; agents see their own project only

session.bootstrap.summary: Who am I, who else is here, and what may I call: the one call every agent makes first

session.update.summary: Patch a session; branch/model/effort conflict after first spawn

session.report.summary: Provider hooks calling home: session_start | tool_use | stop | notification | idle | blocked

session.attach.summary: Attach the pty stream, replaying from (epoch, seq)

session.resize.summary: Resize the PTY, for good or until this connection detaches

session.scrollback.summary: Scrollback text, the (epoch, seq) it ends at, and the PTY's size

session.restorable.summary: Sessions offering resume at launch, optionally one project's or one session's

overlap.list.summary: Session pairs sharing changed files / symbols

overlap.flag.summary: An agent claiming 'I am touching this'

guardrail.gate.summary: The enforcement door: hooks call it before a write/commit/exec; may create a hold

guardrail.hold.get.summary: Inspect the frozen action before deciding a hold

guardrail.config.get.summary: Effective guardrail config: defaults, then global, workspace and project overrides

guardrail.config.set.summary: Patch one layer of guardrail config (caps, protected paths, thresholds, roles)

guardrail.config.layers.summary: One guardrail config layer: effective, inherited, its own overrides, and which layer set each value

guardrail.check.summary: Pure dry run of gate: nothing created, nothing audited

guardrail.explain.summary: Preflight a whole plan: which paths, commands and totals would be allowed, held or refused

guardrail.request.summary: Ask the user for a guardrail exception when you cannot progress without one; every agent may call it

guardrail.request.get.summary: One exception request and its grant: open, approved (and whether still active), denied

guardrail.grant.revoke.summary: End an approved exception before it would expire

worktree.create.summary: Create a worktree on a branch

worktree.remove.summary: Remove a worktree; conflict if a session owns it

worktree.disk.summary: Disk per worktree, build output separately

git.diff.file.summary: One file's old/new text and hunks (for @codemirror/merge)

git.branches.summary: Branches with merged flag and session owner for the selected worktree

git.branch.create.summary: Create a branch in a project worktree and optionally check it out

git.branch.switch.summary: Switch a checkout without a live session to a local or remote branch; uncommitted changes are carried or refused, never discarded

git.branch.delete.summary: Delete one merged local branch that is not checked out or owned by a session

git.pr.list.summary: All pull request states for the project, across every page; cached for a minute unless refresh

git.pr.open.summary: Open a PR for the branch

git.branch.clean_merged.summary: Delete merged branches without a live/parked session

git.branch.cleanup.summary: Remove the worktree and branch of every closed session whose work is merged (into the base branch, or by a merged GitHub PR); unmerged work is kept

git.suggest_message.summary: Heuristic commit subject from the diff

integration.request.summary: Octopus-merge N branches into a throwaway worktree, build, optionally deploy; results via events

file.write.summary: Write a file through the guardrails

file.trash.list.summary: Trashed files not yet restored or expired

file.restore_head.summary: git checkout -- <path>: put a tracked file back as HEAD has it

file.import.summary: Copy files in from the OS (drag-in)

device.mirror.input.summary: Touch / key event to the device

avd.list.summary: Installed Android Virtual Devices and running serials

avd.catalog.summary: Installed system images and device profiles available for AVD creation

avd.stop.summary: Shut down a running Android Virtual Device

device.leases.summary: Who is using which Android device right now, without asking adb

device.claim.summary: Hold an Android device across several steps (install, test, inspect) so no other session installs over it; device.busy names the holder

device.release.summary: Release a device lease you hold (the user may release any lease but a live run's)

provider.update.summary: Update a supported user-installed provider in the background

usage.get.summary: Per-provider usage in its own units

usage.report.summary: Provider metering pushed by its statusLine/hook

skill.get.summary: One skill with its whole body

skill.enable.summary: Enable / disable a skill for a project

skill.install.summary: Install or refresh SKILL.md files from a GitHub repository

github.status.summary: GitHub CLI installation and authentication state

settings.get.summary: Settings subtree by dotted path (whole tree if absent)

dashboard.get.summary: Cross-project overview in one round trip

ui.state.summary: The engine's shell model: the last page switched to, plus panes and windows recorded by ui.* ops. Not the native window's own panes

ui.page.switch.summary: Switch the page (and project); the native client follows

ui.pane.open.summary: Record a pane in the shell model. The native client acts only on target.session (it focuses that terminal); other targets open nothing

ui.pane.close.summary: Remove a pane from the shell model; the native client closes nothing

ui.pane.focus.summary: Focus a pane in the shell model; the native client follows only when the pane has target.session

ui.pane.move.summary: Reorder panes in the shell model; the native client does not move anything

ui.layout.save.summary: Save the current arrangement under a name (overwrites)

ui.window.popout.summary: Record a pop-out window in the shell model; no OS window opens

ui.window.close.summary: Remove a pop-out window from the shell model

ui.window.list.summary: Windows in the shell model (main plus recorded pop-outs), not real OS windows

ui.toast.summary: Show text in the native client's notice bar (emits ui.toast; level and ttl_ms are carried but ignored)

os.open_url.summary: Open a URL in the system browser

id.description: UUID v4 minted by the caller; idempotency key for 24h.

payload.description: Op-specific; `{}` when the op takes nothing.

token.description: Session token binding an `agent:<name>` actor on the socket door.

Actor.description: "user" | "agent:<session-name>" | "test" ("system" is internal and rejected at every door)

id.description: `null` only when the request could not be parsed far enough to read one (`bus.parse`).

replayed.description: Present (true) when the id was seen before and the recorded result was returned.

mail.description: Live, unaudited sideband. Present only when an authenticated agent has priority mail.

message.description: Human sentence; may change; never parse it.

Confirm.description: The op that lifts a hold (present iff `kind == held`).

priority.description: Number of unread priority messages for the authenticated agent session.

MailHint.description: A response envelope (BUS.md §1.2). Exactly one of `result` / `error` is present.

cause.description: Request id that caused it; absent for system-originated events.

Event.description: A fact about a mutation that already happened (BUS.md §1.3).

stream.description:
`pty` | `logcat` | `mirror`, all on the socket door (BUS.md §7). `app.log.tail` declares
a `log` stream but sends no frames yet.

mirror_id.description: `mirror` only: which `device.mirror.start` this frame belongs to.

epoch.description: `pty` only: increments on every spawn/wake; `seq` restarts at 0 within it.

data.description:
base64 for `pty`; a line for `logcat`; for `mirror`, a base64 video packet or a status
object (state, picture size, device, and the typed reason on the last one).

Frame.description: A data-plane frame (BUS.md §7) as carried on the socket door.

implemented.description: Whether the running engine has a handler for it (else `bus.not_implemented`).

call.description:
All-layers verdict for the asking actor. `None` when nothing evaluated it (the static
schema render), so a reader never mistakes "not computed" for "callable".

why.description: Which layer decided `call`, in one phrase.

oneOf.description: Everyone may call it, but the op exists *for* agents (self-report style).

Doors.description:
Which doors carry an op. A `socket_only` op acts on the connection that sends it (a
subscriber, a wait), so the socket door answers it; the engine refuses it with `bus.door`.

oneOf.description: Callable, but only for the actor's own session (or its PAIR partner, for reads).

Callable.description:
Whether the asking actor may really call an op, across all three gating layers
(registry `actors`, runtime row scope, and the role allowlist). `bus.ops` reports it.

can_call.description: Every op this actor may really call, all three gating layers applied.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots this actor may write to, worktree first.

events.description: Exact names or `prefix.*`. Empty waits for anything.

timeout_ms.description: How long to block before giving up. Default 60s, clamped to an hour.

matching.description:
Only an event whose payload has every one of these top-level keys equal to the value
given, e.g. `{"request_id": 7}`. Omit to take the first event that matches by name.

spawn_profile.description: How Relay spawns it: flags, env, hook file layout. Opaque, for display and diagnosis.

guarded.description:
Whether this provider supports Relay's `PreToolUse` guardrail and lifecycle adapters.
Provider-native trust may still require one explicit approval before a generated hook runs.

payload.description: `null` when the payload was larger than 64 KiB.

expect.description: `{updated_at}` of the entity after the op; `audit.undo` refuses on mismatch (§5.5).

force.description:
Also remove every project in it, closing their open sessions (`project.remove` with `force`).
Without it the op refuses `workspace.has_projects`.

remove_worktrees.description:
With `force`: also delete the Relay-pool worktrees of the sessions it closes. Branches
are always kept; off by default, so every checkout stays on disk.

force.description:
Close its open sessions (`session.close`, worktree kept) and stop its device runs first.
Without it the op refuses `project.sessions_live` / `project.activity_live`.

remove_worktrees.description:
With `force`: also delete the Relay-pool worktrees of the sessions it closes. Branches
are always kept; off by default, so every checkout stays on disk.

parent_id.description: Create it straight as a sub-task of this one; refused past `TASK_DEPTH_MAX`.

labels.description: Free-form tags; unknown names are created in the project's label set.

TaskState.description: Agent lifecycle on a task, independent of column (BUS.md §11.1, confirmed 2026-08-17).

TaskType.description:
A first-class classification, separate from the free-form `labels` (BUS.md §11.1).
`Task` is the neutral default and is what every pre-v16 row migrated to; the other four
are the vocabulary the board filters on.

parent_id.description: Parent task, if this is a sub-task. Nesting is capped at [`TASK_DEPTH_MAX`] levels.

depth.description: 0 for a root task, 1 for its child, and so on — never above `TASK_DEPTH_MAX - 1`.

children.description: Direct children, in board order. Children stay real tasks with their own cards.

rollup.description: Progress over the whole subtree, for the parent's `n/m done` badge.

labels.description: Free-form tags, sorted; the supplementary layer under `type`.

blocked_by.description: Tasks this one waits on (stored edges).

blocks.description: Tasks waiting on this one (the inverse read of `blocked_by`).

duplicate_of.description: The task this duplicates, if any.

sessions.description: Every session ever dispatched to it, in order; a PAIR adds two.

TaskRollup.description:
Roll-up of a parent's descendants (BUS.md §11.1). Counts the whole subtree, not just the
direct children, so a grandparent reads as one body of work. Zero `total` = a leaf.

path.description: Path under the store's attachment dir.

label.description: One label name, exact and case-insensitive.

session.description: A session name; matches every task that session was ever dispatched to.

parent_id.description: `Some(Some(id))` = children of that task, `Some(None)` = roots only, absent = every task.

limit.description:
Page size, default 1000, at most 2000. Done cards sort last, so a page cut short drops
the oldest finished work first.

offset.description: Skip this many tasks of the ordered result: the previous page's `next_offset`.

summary.description: Leave each task's `body` and `changelog` empty: a board needs titles, not essays.

next_offset.description: Set when more tasks match than this page holds: pass it as `offset`.

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

parent_id.description: Absent or null detaches the task back to a root.

Label.description: A free-form supplementary tag, scoped to a project. Types classify; labels annotate.

TaskRelation.description:
Task-to-task edges other than parent/child (BUS.md §11.1). Only these two are stored;
`blocks` is the inverse read of `blocked_by` and never has a row of its own.

fanout.description: Also dispatch every not-done descendant, one fresh session each. Requires `create`.

start.description:
Defaults to true. False stages the assignment without starting the provider, so a
multi-task launch can attach its complete queue before the first agent turn.

worktree.description: `"new"` (default: pooled worktree), `"primary"`, or an absolute path of an existing worktree.

prompt.description: Persist the initial assignment before spawning, so a partial launch can recover it.

intent.description: One line of what this session is doing, in its own words (`session.intent`).

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

include_deleted.description: Also list soft-deleted notes (`deleted_at` set), which `notes.restore` brings back.

summary.description: Cut each `body` to a preview of its first 240 characters; `notes.get` has the whole note.

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

delivery.description:
`queued` (at least one addressee is live), `session_parked` (all parked),
`not_running` (all created or exited), or `no_recipients` (an empty broadcast).

state.description:
The recipient session's state right now: `running` will see it, `parked` will not
until it wakes.

before.description: Only messages older than this message id: the previous page's `next_before`.

messages.description: Oldest first. Without `unread_only` this is the newest page; with it, the oldest unread.

next_before.description: Set when older messages remain: pass it as `before` for the page before this one.

more_unread.description: More unread messages remain past this page (`unread_only`): ack these, then ask again.

prompt.description: Omitted preserves the allocated assignment; an empty string explicitly clears it.

status.description:
`completed` (default), `blocked`, or `partial`. An op that can only report success
gets reported success (D118).

text.description: One line, present tense. Empty clears it.

paths.description: Worktree-relative paths this session is taking on.

symbol.description: Narrow the claim to one symbol within each path.

exclusive.description:
Refuse the whole claim if any path is already claimed by a peer, instead of recording
it alongside theirs and reporting the collision.

collisions.description: Peers already holding one of these paths. Empty is the quiet, expected case.

paths.description: Omit to release every claim this session holds.

intent.description:
One line of what this peer is doing, in its own words (`session.intent`). Coordination
needs to know what a peer is *up to*, which no amount of state and branch names says.

text.description: Everything, skills included. What the UI shows.

compact.description:
State, peers, notes and adjacent work only — the part small enough to inject on every
spawn. Skill bodies are referenced by path instead of inlined (D101).

task.description: Current task retained for older clients and one-task agents.

tasks.description: Current task followed by every queued or in-review task attached to this session.

brief_path.description: Worktree-relative path of the full brief.

peers.description: Everyone else live in this project, now.

can_call.description: Every op this session may really call, all three gating layers applied.

discovery.description: How to inspect operation summaries and exact payload/result schemas without guessing.

comms.description: How to reach the peers above, and which channel actually reaches all of them.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots this session may write to, worktree first.

dry_run.description: The op that answers "would this be allowed?" without doing it.

exceptions.description:
What to do when a refusal stands between you and the task: how to ask the user for an
exception and wait for the answer.

until_detach.description:
Borrow the size: on a connection door, the PTY goes back to the size it had when this
connection detaches from the session or goes away, unless someone resized it since.

cols.description: The live PTY's size; absent when the text comes from a saved scrollback.

project_id.description:
Only this project's sessions. Each one costs a `git status` of its worktree, so a
client describing one project's panes should not pay for every project's (RA-235).

full.description:
Return every string whole, however large. By default a string over 64 KiB in the
payload or details is cut to its first 4 KiB and named in `elided`.

request.description:
The exact frozen action, with authentication material removed. `guardrail.confirm`
replays the stored action whole, whatever was elided here.

elided.description: JSON pointers (`/request/payload/new_text`, `/hold/details/reason`) of the strings cut short.

scope.description: Exception requests only: how long the grant lasts. Defaults to what the agent asked for.

GrantScope.description: How long an approved exception lasts: one use, or until the session ends.

workspace_id.description: One of the two, or neither for the global layer.

denied_commands.description:
Command patterns refused for `kind: exec`. Matched against the *parsed argv* of each
command in the line, never as a raw substring, so quoted data mentioning one is fine.

allowed_write_roots.description:
Absolute roots an agent may write to outside its worktree — scratch space, which is
not a repo-integrity concern. `$TMPDIR` is always honoured in addition to these.

agent_builds.description:
Whether an agent's `integration.request` may run the project's build command without a
person confirming it. Off by default: the build runs outside any sandbox (RA-167), so an
agent's request that builds is held for confirmation; a merge-only request is not.

GuardrailConfig.description: Effective guardrail configuration after global + project merge.

min_file_lines.description:
The percentage rule is skipped for files shorter than this. A percentage of a very
short file measures nothing: one line of a one-line file is 100%.

allow_if_recoverable.description:
Let a large rewrite through when git can put the file back — committed and unmodified,
or ignored entirely. Set false to hold on volume alone.

DestructiveWrite.description: A write is destructive when either threshold is exceeded.

ShapeGate.description: A built-in validator attached to one critical, worktree-relative path.

RoleAllowlist.description: Role allow-sets are configurable, but the defaults are the baseline in BUS.md §9.1.

workspace_id.description: Patch this workspace's layer. At most one of `workspace_id` / `project_id`.

patch.description: Merged into the layer's stored overrides; `null` clears a key back to the inherited value.

workspace_id.description: At most one of the two; neither reads the global layer.

inherited.description: What this layer would get with no overrides of its own: the parent layer's effective config.

overrides.description: This layer's stored overrides, exactly as stored.

sources.description: Leaf path (`caps.files`, `protected_paths`) to the layer that decided its value.

GuardrailLayer.description:
Which layer of guardrail configuration a value lives in. Each layer overrides the one
before it: defaults, then global, then the project's workspace, then the project.

paths.description: Worktree-relative paths the plan intends to touch.

lines.description: Lines the plan expects to change in total, if known.

commands.description: Commands the plan intends to run.

verdict.description: The worst verdict across everything below.

files.description: What the plan costs against the commit caps.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots the caller may write to.

policy.description: The policy that decided it, when one did.

kind.description:
`command` for a denied command, `path` for a protected path / write root / large rewrite,
`cap` for the commit caps.

value.description: The exact command line; the path (worktree-relative or absolute); or `files=N lines=M`.

reason.description: Why you cannot progress without it. The user reads this before deciding.

scope.description: What you are asking for; the user may grant less. Default `once`.

ExceptionKind.description:
What an agent asks to be let past. `command` lifts a denied command, `path` a protected
path, a write root or a destructive-write rule, `cap` the commit caps.

created.description: False when an identical request from this session was already open.

wait_for.description: The event announcing the answer; wait with `bus.wait {events:[wait_for], matching:{request_id}}`.

id.description:
Also the id of the hold that carries it, so `guardrail.confirm` / `guardrail.reject`
answer it with `hold_id` set to this.

value.description:
The exact command, the path (worktree-relative, a glob, or an absolute root), or the
caps wanted (`files=N lines=M`; empty lifts the caps for the grant's life).

active.description: Approved, not revoked, and (for `once`) not yet used.

GuardrailException.description: An agent's request to be let past one guardrail, and — once a person answered — the grant.

files.description:
A wholly untracked directory is one entry, its path ending in `/`. At most a few thousand
entries: conflicts first, then other tracked changes, then untracked ones.

truncated.description: Whether `files` stops short of every change git reported.

total.description: How many entries git reported, `files` included; more than `files.len()` when truncated.

staged.description: Compare with the index, what a commit would record, instead of the working tree.

old_path.description: For a rename, the file's path in the old side (`renamed_from` in `git.status`).

branch.description: The branch name on the remote, `feature`.

local.description: The local branch of the same name, if there is one; switching to the remote selects it.

name.description:
A local branch, or a remote-tracking one (`origin/feature`) to check out as a new local
tracking branch.

carry_changes.description:
Bring uncommitted changes to tracked files along, as `git switch` does. Git still refuses
when the target branch would overwrite them; nothing is ever discarded.

branch.description: The local branch now checked out.

created.description: Whether a local tracking branch was created for a remote branch.

refresh.description:
Ask GitHub now instead of answering from the last listing (kept up to a minute, and
dropped by `git.push` and `git.pr.open`). For an explicit refresh, not for every redraw.

session.description: The closed session that worked on it.

reason.description: Why: how the work was found merged, or what unmerged work kept it.

limit.description: Most entries listed per directory, default 2000, at most 5000.

truncated.description:
Directories cut short at `limit`, by worktree-relative path, with how many entries each
really holds. Ask for one again with its `path` and a larger `limit` to see more.

worktree.description: The checkout it was deleted from, and where `file.restore` puts it back.

available.description: Whether the trashed bytes are still on disk.

col.description: 1-based byte offset of the match in the whole line.

text.description: The line, or for a long one a window of it around the match.

text_offset.description:
Set when `text` is a window: the byte offset in the line where it starts, so the match
begins `col - 1 - text_offset` bytes into `text`.

lease.description:
Who is using this device right now, if anyone. A conflicting run, install or claim
from anyone else is refused with `device.busy` until it is released.

device.description:
The device serial, or `*` when the command named no device (adb's only device, or
Gradle's every device): that lease conflicts with every device.

session.description: The holding session's name; `None` when the user holds it directly.

action.description:
What the holder is doing, in a few words (`device.run debug from relay/brisk-otter`,
`adb install app-debug.apk`).

expires_in_s.description: Seconds until the lease lapses on its own; `None` while it lasts as long as its run.

DeviceLease.description:
One holder's exclusive use of an Android device: a `device.run` in flight, an agent's
`adb install` / `gradlew install*` seen by the guardrail hook, or an explicit `device.claim`.
Released with a `device.lease.released` event, so `bus.wait` can wait for it.

kind.description:
`run` installs and launches on `device`; `build` produces an artifact and
leaves `device` empty (D152).

artifact.description: Absolute path of the APK / AAB a finished `build` produced.

variant.description: Gradle variant and artifact format for a release build; absent for device runs.

publish.description: True when this build was also handed to Gradle Play Publisher.

signing.description: `signed`, `unsigned`, or `unverified` after Relay inspects the artifact.

device.description: Serial from `device.list`; omit to claim every device (what a bare `adb` would touch).

action.description: What you will be doing, shown to anyone refused with `device.busy`.

minutes.description: How long to hold it. Default 10, at most 60; released early by `device.release`.

device.description: Serial to release; omit to release every lease you hold.

windows.description: Provider's own units and windows, opaque; the UI knows each provider's shape.

summary.description:
Cut each body to its opening, frontmatter included, instead of the whole SKILL.md;
`skill.get` returns one whole body.

source_ref.description:
The branch or tag a GitHub skill was installed from; `None` is the repository's
default branch (or a local skill). A refresh pulls this ref again.

Branch or tag to clone; overrides one named by a `tree/<ref>` URL. When neither names
one and `subdir` is an installed skill's `source_path`, its recorded `source_ref` is
kept, so "Update from GitHub" stays on the branch the skill came from.

replace_skill_id.description:
Explicit permission to replace one visible skill when its name conflicts with the
downloaded SKILL.md. Hidden soft-deleted rows are reclaimed automatically.

docs.description: Documentation files, relative to the plugin root; `plugin.get` returns their text.

enabled_in.description: Projects the plugin is switched on for.

suggested_for.description:
Projects whose checkout looks like this plugin's kind of project (for Unreal Engine, a
`.uproject` at the root) and that do not have it on yet.

Plugin.description:
A plugin bundled with Relay: skills, always-on agent instructions, documentation and MCP
servers that reach every agent of a project the plugin is switched on for (D159).

name.description: The skill's folder name, which is also its provider-visible name.

files.description: Files in the skill folder, `SKILL.md` included.

instructions.description: The instructions every agent of an enabled project receives in its brief.

link.description: Deep link: an op to run when clicked.

PaneTarget.description: What a pane shows; shape depends on `PaneKind`.
